prompt.context_jp: 雨宮蛍の頭の中では、ある声____いつまでも繰り返し響いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 雨宮蛍の頭の中では、ある声____いつまでも繰り返し響いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits.

feedback.correct_en: 「ある声」is newly introduced information — the narrator is telling us a voice exists in her head. New-information subjects in narration typically take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 'the voice' as already-established topic, but the voice is being introduced here. を doesn't fit with 響く (intransitive).

contrast_examples.jp: その声は消えなかった。
contrast_examples.en: That voice didn't fade. (already known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 上司の高野誠一に突きつけられた言葉____、どれほど打ち消そうとしても消えてくれない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 上司の高野誠一に突きつけられた言葉____、どれほど打ち消そうとしても消えてくれない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence makes '上司に突きつけられた言葉' the topic and comments on it ('no matter how she tries, it won't disappear'). This topic-comment structure needs は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as new information, but the words were just mentioned in the prior sentence — they're the established topic now.

contrast_examples.en: Words suddenly came to mind. (new event)

prompt.context_jp: その日も、インテリアデザイン事業部のフロア____は朝から慌ただしい空気が流れていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: インテリアデザイン事業部のフロア____は朝から慌ただしい空気が流れていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits.

feedback.correct_en: 流れる (to flow/hang in the air) takes に to mark where the atmosphere exists/hangs. に + は contrasts the floor with other places.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the location of an action, but 流れる here describes a state of existence (atmosphere hanging there), which pairs with に.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋に静けさが流れる。

contrast_examples.en: We held a meeting on the floor. (action location)

prompt.context_jp: けれど会社にいる間の彼女____、少なくとも見た目だけは、きちんとした一人前の社員だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: けれど会社にいる間の彼女____、少なくとも見た目だけは、きちんとした一人前の社員だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits.

feedback.correct_en: 「けれど」signals contrast with her slovenly private self. は marks '彼女 while at the office' as the contrastive topic — at least this version of her looks proper.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce her as new information, losing the contrastive nuance against her home self.

contrast_examples.jp: 家では だらしないが、会社では きちんとしている。
contrast_examples.en: At home she's sloppy, but at work she's proper. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 午後になると、高野のデスクの周り____事業部の面々が集まってきた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 高野のデスクの周り____事業部の面々が集まってきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits.

feedback.correct_en: 集まる (to gather) marks the destination/convergence point with に. People gathered 'to' around the desk.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the location of an ongoing action, but 集まる emphasizes movement/arrival to a point, which takes に.

prompt.context_jp: 部長の短い問いかけに、その場の空気____少しだけ張り詰めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部長の短い問いかけに、その場の空気____少しだけ張り詰めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits.

feedback.correct_en: This reports an event happening in the scene — the air became tense. Event-reporting subjects take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the air as a known topic needing comment, but here we're reporting an observable change in the scene.

contrast_examples.jp: 急に空気が張り詰めた。

contrast_examples.en: The atmosphere is always heavy. (generic statement)

prompt.context_jp: 「地の利____ とてもいいんです｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「地の利____ とてもいいんです｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits Hotaru's sales pitch.

feedback.correct_en: Hotaru is commenting ON the shop's location as a known feature: 'as for the location, it's great.' This topic-comment pattern with evaluation takes は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal 'the location (as opposed to something else) is good' — an exhaustive reading that doesn't fit her relaxed pitch.

contrast_examples.jp: 地の利がいいのが強み。
contrast_examples.en: IT'S the location that's the strong point. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 「自信____ どうだ？ ＯＬの話題になるような 新しい店をつくる自信____あるか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「自信____ どうだ？ 新しい店をつくる自信____あるか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Both blanks take the SAME particle — choose it.

feedback.correct_en: Takano picks up 自信 as the topic ('as for confidence, how about it?') and questions its existence. ある with topicalized nouns typically uses は in such 'do you have X?' probes.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would focus-mark confidence as new information, but Takano is zeroing in on it as the discussion topic.

contrast_examples.jp: 自信がある人は手を挙げて。
contrast_examples.en: Those who have confidence, raise your hand. (relative clause—が)

prompt.context_jp: 山田に言われたリサーチをまとめながらも、蛍の手____たびたび止まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蛍の手____たびたび止まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits.

feedback.correct_en: This narrates an event happening to a part of Hotaru — her hands keep stopping. Body-part subjects in event descriptions normally take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make '蛍の手' a contrastive topic, suggesting 'her hands (unlike something else) stopped,' which doesn't match the narrative flow.

prompt.context_jp: 画面の文字____、さっきから少しも進んでいない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 画面の文字____、さっきから少しも進んでいない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The text on the screen is the topic being commented on negatively ('hasn't advanced at all'). は fits topic+negative-comment patterns, often with a contrastive feel (unlike her mind, which races).
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the text as new info, but it's the ongoing subject being reflected on.

contrast_examples.en: The text isn't progressing. (comment on topic)

prompt.context_jp: 送り主の名前が目に飛び込んできた瞬間、指先____ぴたりと止まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 指先____ぴたりと止まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: An event happening to her fingertip in the scene — new, observed happening. Narrative events with body-part subjects take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would need prior topic establishment of her fingertip; here it's the fresh detail being reported.

prompt.context_jp: 恋の経験____乏しいことが、これほどもどかしく感じられたことはなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 恋の経験____乏しいことが、これほどもどかしく感じられたことはなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a noun-modifying clause (「...こと」), the subject normally takes が, not は. 恋の経験 is the subject of 乏しい within that embedded clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は rarely appears inside relative/noun-modifying clauses as the subject marker; it would also strip the clause of its tight predicate connection.

contrast_examples.jp: 経験が乏しいことに気づいた。
contrast_examples.en: I noticed my experience is scarce. (embedded—が)

prompt.context_jp: 振り向くと、高野____険しい顔つきで立っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 振り向くと、高野____険しい顔つきで立っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: After 振り向くと, Takano is being newly presented into the scene (she turns and 'there was Takano'). Discovery/presentation uses が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame Takano as already-established topic, losing the 'oh, there he is' discovery feel.

contrast_examples.en: When I turned around, there he was. (discovery)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼はそこに立っていた。

prompt.context_jp: 「だったら 部長____ やってくださいよ｡ 部長のほうが力あるんだから｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「だったら 部長____ やってくださいよ｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Hotaru is pushing the task back exhaustively: '(as opposed to me) YOU, boss, should do it.' This exclusive/identifying contrast uses が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a mild topic-comment, losing the pointed 'you specifically, not me' nuance that fits her protest.

contrast_examples.jp: 部長がやってください。
部長はやらないんですか。
contrast_examples.en: Aren't you going to do it, boss? (topic question)

prompt.context_jp: 庭の木々が大きくしなり、風の音____急に強くなってきた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 風の音____急に強くなってきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: A new event enters the scene — the wind's sound suddenly grew loud. Sensory event reports take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would set the sound as a known topic, but this is a fresh change the characters notice.

contrast_examples.en: The sound of wind is scary. (general)

prompt.context_jp: マコトが席を外すと、フロア____は優華と神宮司だけが残された。
prompt.prompt_jp: マコトが席を外すと、フロア____は優華と神宮司だけが残された。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 残される describes a state of existing/remaining at a location. Existence-location takes に + は (contrastive 'on the floor, only...').
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the venue of an action, but 残る here describes being left in place — a stative location taking に.

prompt.context_jp: 「昨日 店に立ち寄った際に ____が落ちているようなので リノベーションは どうかと…｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「____が落ちているようなので リノベーションは どうかと…｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that collocates naturally.

feedback.correct_en: 客足が落ちる is the standard collocation meaning 'customer traffic drops.' Teshima uses this business idiom to diagnose the bakery.
feedback.incorrect_en: 客道 and 客場 aren't real words in this sense. Only 客足 pairs with 落ちる in business Japanese.

prompt.context_jp: 「ＯＬの____は バカにできないからね｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ＯＬの____は バカにできないからね｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the natural term for word-of-mouth.

feedback.correct_en: 口コミ means 'word of mouth' — the marketing concept the dept head is invoking. 'ＯＬの口コミ' = buzz from office-ladies.
feedback.incorrect_en: 口答え means 'talking back,' 口上 means a formal speech/pitch — neither fits a marketing-reach context.

prompt.context_jp: 蛍は小さく息を____、再び受話器を取る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蛍は小さく息を____、再び受話器を取る。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with 息を.

feedback.correct_en: 息を整える = 'to steady one's breath.' This is the fixed collocation for composing oneself before action.
feedback.incorrect_en: 息を伸ばす / 広げる aren't natural collocations. Breath is 'ordered/arranged' (整える), not stretched or spread.

contrast_examples.jp: 息を整えて話し始めた。
contrast_examples.en: He steadied his breath and began to speak.

prompt.context_jp: 「何にも考えないで ____ 返信するようでは 女として 問題外！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「何にも考えないで ____ 返信するようでは…」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word meaning 'immediately / right away.'

feedback.correct_en: 即行 (そっこう) is colloquial for 'right away / immediately,' matching Yamada's warning against instant replies.
feedback.incorrect_en: 即売 means 'spot sale,' 即物 means 'materialistic/concrete' — neither works for 'replying right away.'

prompt.context_jp: 「____たたいてた割には 大したことないな｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「____たたいてた割には 大したことないな｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that forms the idiom 'to brag/talk big.'

feedback.correct_en: 大口をたたく is the set idiom for 'to brag / talk big.' Takano is criticizing Makoto for boasting but delivering little.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大声 (loud voice) and 大手 (major company) don't pair with たたく in this idiomatic sense.

prompt.context_jp: 「間に合わなかったら ____ し｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「間に合わなかったら ____ し｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word meaning 'pitiful / feel sorry for.'

feedback.correct_en: かわいそう = 'poor thing / I feel bad for him.' Hotaru is expressing sympathy for Makoto's situation.
feedback.incorrect_en: かわいらしい means 'cute,' かわった means 'strange' — neither fits a 'I'd feel sorry' context.

contrast_examples.en: I feel sorry for the cat.

prompt.context_jp: 「何か こう ____ってのも 必要なんですけどね｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「何か こう ____の転換ってのも 必要なんですけどね｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word meaning 'change of perspective/approach.'

feedback.correct_en: 発想の転換 = 'a change in thinking/approach' — a common phrase for creative work. It's what Makoto needs.
feedback.incorrect_en: 発表 (announcement) and 発車 (vehicle departure) don't collocate with 転換 in this creative-thinking sense.

contrast_examples.en: We need a shift in thinking.

prompt.context_jp: 「一緒に暮らしてることがバレたら 立場上 こっちだって困る｡ 玄関で____！」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'stop/block (someone) at the door.'

feedback.correct_en: 食い止める = 'to stop / hold back.' Takano is telling Hotaru to prevent Makoto from entering past the entrance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 食べ切る means 'finish eating,' 食い違う means 'to differ/clash' — neither fits 'block him at the door.'

prompt.context_jp: Hotaru answers Takano's question about whether Teshima can pull off the renovation. She wants to express confidence in Teshima specifically.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Hotaru's vote of confidence?

choices.text: 手嶋さんなら 大丈夫だと思います。
手嶋さんは 大丈夫だと思います、たぶん。
手嶋さんが 大丈夫だと思います。

feedback.correct_en: The …なら construction ('if it's Teshima') is the natural way to vouch exclusively for a specific person. This is the line as actually spoken in the story.
feedback.incorrect_en: B weakens the vote with 'probably,' undermining the endorsement. C uses が awkwardly — が marks the subject of 思う but sounds off here; …なら is the idiomatic endorsement frame.

contrast_examples.en: If it's him, it'll be fine. (confident endorsement)

prompt.context_jp: Hotaru is explaining Yamada's 'question-form reply' trick to Takano. She wants to give an example.
prompt.prompt_en: Which example line is the most natural illustration of the 疑問系 trick?

feedback.correct_en: 「今 何時？」is the casual, natural phrasing for a chatty text — exactly the register Hotaru uses in the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is overly formal and stilted for a texting trick. C has unnatural word order — Japanese prefers the time-word first (何時).

contrast_examples.en: What time is it now? (natural casual)

prompt.context_jp: Hotaru wants Takano to repeat his encouraging line because it made her happy.
prompt.prompt_en: Which request sounds most natural in this warm, slightly shy moment?

choices.text: 嬉しかったので もう1回 いってください。
嬉しいだから もう1回 いってください。
嬉しくて もう1回 いえ。

feedback.correct_en: 嬉しかったので … ください is natural polite request with a past reason — the exact line Hotaru uses.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is ungrammatical (嬉しいだから is wrong; adjectives don't take だ before から). C uses the blunt imperative いえ, far too rough toward one's boss.

contrast_examples.jp: 嬉しかったので、もう一度言ってください。
contrast_examples.en: Because I was happy, please say it again.

prompt.context_jp: Hotaru finally composes her careful work-style email to Teshima about the reference materials.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as a polite, work-register note?

choices.text: 雨宮です。参考資料まとめました。良かったら見てください。
雨宮だ。参考資料まとめたよ。見ろ。
雨宮と申し上げます。参考資料をまとめた次第でございまして、ご覧くださいませ。

feedback.correct_en: A matches the polite-but-not-stiff workplace register Hotaru settles on — exactly the line in the story.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is blunt/casual and inappropriate to a colleague she admires. C is excessively honorific/keigo, wrong tone for peer-to-peer work mail.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨宮です。資料まとめました。
contrast_examples.en: This is Amemiya. I compiled the materials. (business-casual)
I am Amemiya. (over-formal for colleague mail)

prompt.context_jp: Hotaru asks Takano if people really can change, hoping for reassurance.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for this hopeful, tentative question?

choices.text: 人は 変われますよね？
人は 変えられますよね？
人は 変わるでしょうか、たぶん？

feedback.correct_en: 変われる is the potential form of 変わる ('be able to change oneself'), and ～よね？ seeks gentle agreement — exactly Hotaru's wistful hope.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses 変えられる (can be changed by someone else) — a passive/causative nuance that changes the meaning. C mixes でしょうか and たぶん awkwardly.
